name: Herpa Lufthansa Airbus A350-900 "100 Jahre" Reg: D-AIXL HE539012 Scale 1:500
description:
Herpa Wings Lufthansa Airbus A350-900 "100 Jahre" Reg: D-AIXL HE539012 Scale 1:500
In 2026, Lufthansa will celebrate a significant anniversary: 100 years since the founding of the first Lufthansa back in 1926. To mark this special occasion, the airline with its unmistakable crane logo will take off with a unique "anniversary fleet": Lufthansa's most important sub-fleets will receive their own special livery in the iconic centenary look: The blue fuselage will be adorned with a white crane whose wings merge into the aircraft wings. The anniversary fleet will be led by the brand-new Boeing 787-9 "Berlin" with the registration D-ABPU, which we have already announced in a total of three versions in the 1/500 and 1/200 scales. Next up is an Airbus A350-900, which is also already in development as a die-cast metal model in 1/500, as a high-quality collector's model in 1/200, and as part of the Herpa SnapFit range, also in the 1/200 scale.
Dimensions: 5.3" L x 5.1" W (13.4 x 13.0 cm)
Material: Diecast metal with some plastic parts
Accessories: None

description:

GeminiJets proudly introduces the Gemini200 1:200-scale Antonov Airlines An-225, item G2ADB1225. Once the largest aircraft in the world, the Antonov 225 was destroyed in Ukraine one year ago today. name: Herpa Lufthansa Boeing 787-9 "100 Jahre, Berlin" Reg: D-ABPU HE538947 Scale 1:500
description:
Herpa Wings Lufthansa Boeing 787-9 "100 Jahre, Berlin" Reg: D-ABPU HE538947 Scale 1:500
The stylized crane, now famous worldwide, first took off in 1919 for the Deutsche Luft-Reederei. Seven years later, on April 6, 1926, Deutsche Luft Hansa was founded in Berlin through the merger of the two airlines Deutscher Aero Lloyd and Junkers Luftverkehr. The name was intended to recall the Hanseatic League, the historically significant association of German merchants in the Middle Ages. To mark its 100th anniversary in 2026, Lufthansa has unveiled a Dreamliner in a unique design. The special livery features a blue fuselage with a white crane hovering above, its wings merging into the wings of the aircraft. This makes the wings of the aircraft appear to be the wings of the crane. Designed as a trademark by graphic designer and architect Otto Firle back in 1918, the crane has become Lufthansa's unmistakable symbol worldwide over the decades. The Boeing 787-9 with the registration D-ABPU is scheduled to enter regular service in December, heralding the start of the centenary in 2026. This extraordinary Dreamliner is available from Herpa as a high-quality, fully-assembled model for even the most demanding collectors in the 1/500 and 1/200 scales, as well as part of the extremely popular SnapFit series as an easy-to-assemble push-fit model.
Dimensions: 4.9" L x 4.7" W (12.6 x 12.0 cm)
Material: Diecast metal with some plastic parts
Accessories: None

name: InFlight200 SOFIA 747SP N747NA IF747SPSOFIA02 1:200
description:
Inflight200 SOFIA 747SP N747NA IF747SPSOFIA02 1:200 with stand and key chain
On Wednesday, September 28, at around 8:45pm local time, N747NA the modified NASA Boeing 747SP carrying the reflecting telescope for the Stratospheric Observatory for Infrared Astronomy (SOFIA), operated its last flight ever. The flight lasted 7 hours and 57 minutes, departing from Palmdale Airport (PMD), and flying around the North Pacific Ocean.
N747NA started life with Pan Am in May 1977 and was registered N536PA named Clipper Lindberg. February 1986 saw a change of ownership to United Airlines until October 1987 where the airframe was sold the NASA / Stratospheric Observatory for Infrared Astronomy where the titles were added over the United scheme. December 2004 it was reregistered N747NA and went for the refit on the airframe for the telescope and then emerged with the new NASA scheme which the aircraft retired in still wearing the Clipper Lindberg name.
To commemorate the achievements of this aircraft both models will be made in limited numbers and will both come with a key chain.

name: Herpa Condor Boeing 757-300 "Island" Reg: D-ABOL HE538213 Scale 1:500
description:
Herpa Wings Condor Boeing 757-300 "Island" Reg: D-ABOL HE538213 Scale 1:500
In the mid-1970s, Boeing set about developing a successor to its medium-haul bestseller, the 727 trijet. The result was the twin-engine 757, which promised better performance and greater efficiency. Between 1981 and 2004, no fewer than 1,050 aircraft were to leave the Boeing assembly lines. A variant stretched by seven meters followed, intended especially for medium-haul routes with high demand, such as those served by the German vacation airline Condor. That variant was the 757-300, which has an overall length of 54.4 meters (178 ft) and is certified for up to 295 passengers in a single-class seating configuration. The first customer, Condor, received 15 of these aircraft from 1999 and was the largest operator of this variant alongside Continental Airlines and Delta Air Lines. According to current plans, Condor's remaining eight 757-300s are to be retired by the end of 2025 and replaced by new Airbus A321neo aircraft, the first of which have already entered the fleet. Four of these aircraft have been given the eye-catching new livery. In the case of D-ABOL, the blue stripes are intended to whet the appetite for the sea and are sure to put holidaymakers in a good mood already before their departure.

name: Skymarks United Airlines Boeing 787-10 SKF002 Scale 1:200
description:
SkyMarks Flight United Airlines Boeing 787-10 SKF002 Scale 1:200
This injection-molded plastic airplane model with plastic display stand is faithfully painted in Southwest Airline's livery adding to its authenticity. Made in 1/200 scale, the model features highly detailed graphics, and includes easy-snap pieces so it assembles in minutes. Recommended for ages 14+.
United Airlines was the first airline to operate all three variants of the Boeing 787 Dreamliner family, including the 787-10 which is the largest of the 787 family. It measures 224 feet long by 56 feet high and has a wingspan of 197 feet. It can reach a speed of 593 mph with a range of approximately 6,430 nautical miles, and can fly as high as a maximum altitude of 12,500 feet.
In 2019, United Airlines revised their livery as a tribute to its previous liveries with some added touches to celebrate the heights still yet to come. Retaining the prior livery's globe design, it was repainted light blue instead of gold, while the tail has also been lightened. Additionally, the airline's name is now significantly larger.

name: Herpa Icelandair Boeing 757-300 "100 Years Icelandic Independence" Reg: TF-ISX "Þingvellir" HE538237 Scale 1:500
description:
Icelandair Boeing 757-300 "100 Years Icelandic Independence" Reg: TF-ISX "Þingvellir" HE538237 Scale 1:500
Back in the 1970s, Boeing set about developing a successor to its medium-haul bestseller, the three-engine 727. The result was the twin-engine 757, which promised better performance and greater efficiency. Between 1981 and 2004, no fewer than 1,050 of these aircraft were to leave the Boeing factories. A variant stretched by seven meters followed, especially for medium-haul routes with high demand, such as those served by the German vacation airline Condor. The result was the 757-300, which has an overall length of 54.4 meters and is approved for up to 295 passengers in single-class seating. The first customer, Condor, received 15 of these aircraft from 1999 and was the largest operator of this variant alongside Continental Airlines and Delta Air Lines. In addition to numerous 757-200s, Icelandair currently operates two 757-300s with seating for 223 passengers, one of which, TF-ISX, has been flying Iceland's national colors since 2018 to celebrate 100 years of independence.

name: Herpa Condor Boeing 757-300 "Passion" Reg: D-ABOM HE538893 Scale 1:500
description:
Herpa Wings Condor Boeing 757-300 "Passion" Reg: D-ABOM HE538893 Scale 1:500
A 35-year chapter has come to an end: with a special flight from Frankfurt to Vienna on November 5, 2025, the era of Boeing’s 757 which began back in the year 1990 with the delivery of the first 757-200s came to a close at the German leisure airline. By the end of October, six stretched-fuselage 757-300s were still in service. Among them D-ABOM, which had been given the current livery in January 2023, in this case with the eye-catching stripes in "Passion Red". The 757-300 has already been released in the 1/500 scale in "Island Green", "Sunshine Yellow", and "Sea Blue". This new addition now completes the small series.

name: Herpa Air France Douglas DC-4 Reg: F-BHEH HE571104-001 Scale 1:200
description:
Herpa Wings Air France Douglas DC-4 Reg: F-BHEH HE571104-001 Scale 1:200
The introduction of the Douglas DC-4 opened up new destinations for numerous airlines in the rebuilding period after World War II. First delivered in 1946 – 80 years ago – Air France started Paris-New York flights with the four-engine DC-4, covering the distance with two refueling stops in Shannon, Ireland and Gander, Canada in less than 20 hours. This new addition sports the revised livery introduced in 1950. The main difference was the change from an all-natural-metal finish to a design featuring a white top fuselage. This change was part of a broader trend in aviation at the time, aimed at improving visibility of the Air France logo and titles, helping to distinguish the aircraft and its brand from competitors. Be sure to check out the historically decorated stairs with the legendary winged sea horse (item no. 571876). This set makes a perfect addition to this Douglas DC-4.
Dimensions: 5.6" L x 7.0" W (14.3 x 17.9 cm)
Material: Diecast metal with some plastic parts
Accessories: Display stand

Following the Boeing 787 and Airbus A350, the "Queen of the Skies" is now sporting Lufthansa’s anniversary livery featuring the iconic crane—this time in XXL format. This Boeing 747-8, christened "Niedersachsen", was painted in San Bernardino, California, and completed its first scheduled flight in its new livery on March 6, flying from Frankfurt back to the US west coast — this time to Los Angeles. name: InFlight200 SOFIA 747SP N145UA IF747SPSOFIA01 1:200
description:
Inflight200 SOFIA 747SP N145UA IF747SPSOFIA01 1:200 with stand and key chain 
On Wednesday, September 28, at around 8:45pm local time, N747NA the modified NASA Boeing 747SP carrying the reflecting telescope for the Stratospheric Observatory for Infrared Astronomy (SOFIA), operated its last flight ever. The flight lasted 7 hours and 57 minutes, departing from Palmdale Airport (PMD), and flying around the North Pacific Ocean.
N747NA started life with Pan Am in May 1977 and was registered N536PA named Clipper Lindberg. February 1986 saw a change of ownership to United Airlines until October 1987 where the airframe was sold the NASA / Stratospheric Observatory for Infrared Astronomy where the titles were added over the United scheme. December 2004 it was reregistered N747NA and went for the refit on the airframe for the telescope and then emerged with the new NASA scheme which the aircraft retired in still wearing the Clipper Lindberg name.
To commemorate the achievements of this aircraft both models will be made in limited numbers and will both come with a key chain.

name: InFlight200 Cathay Pacific 777-300ER “Spirit of Hong Kong 80th Anniversary” Reg: B-KQU WB-777-3-024C Scale 1:200
description:
WB Models by InFlight200 Cathay Pacific 777-300ER “Spirit of Hong Kong 80th Anniversary” Reg: B-KQU WB-777-3-024C Scale 1:200
Cathay Pacific celebrates eight decades of service with one of the most artistic special schemes the airline has ever flown — and WB Models brings it home to your collection in precision 1:200 scale.
Unveiled on March 9, 2026 at Hong Kong International Airport, the "Spirit of Hong Kong – 80th Anniversary Edition" livery transforms Boeing 777-300ER B-KQU into a flying canvas. Created in partnership with the West Kowloon Cultural District Authority, the design is the work of Hong Kong multimedia artist Victor Wong, whose generative artwork uses geographical data to render abstract landscapes and colours that flow across the entire fuselage. Inspired by Cathay's award-winning "Gallery in the Skies" Business Class concept, the livery carries both the airline's "80 Years Together" anniversary mark and the WestK logo — a tribute to Hong Kong's cultural identity that now circles the globe on Cathay's flagship long-haul aircraft.
B-KQU itself has served Cathay Pacific since December 2014 and was repainted at Xiamen Taikoo earlier this year before re-entering commercial service in her striking new colours. She joins the airline's retro "lettuce leaf sandwich" A350 (B-LRJ) and 747-8F freighter (B-LJE) as part of a small fleet of commemorative aircraft marking Cathay's 80th anniversary year.
This 1:200 scale diecast from WB Models faithfully reproduces every detail of Victor Wong's artwork, with crisp paint application, accurate panel lines, finely detailed landing gear, and the authentic "80 Years Together" and WestK markings. As with all WB Models releases, this is a strictly limited production — once allocations are filled, no further units will be produced.
A must-have for Cathay Pacific collectors, 777 enthusiasts, and anyone who appreciates the artistry of special liveries.

name: Herpa TWA Trans World Airlines Lockheed L-1649A Jetstream Reg: N8083H HE539364 Scale 1:500
description:
Herpa Wings TWA Trans World Airlines Lockheed L-1649A Jetstream Reg: N8083H HE539364 Scale 1:500
More than six decades after it entered service with TWA back in 1958, N8083H can once again be admired in its original color scheme. It was integrated as a cocktail lounge into the new TWA Hotel, which opened at New York’s JFK Airport in 2019. The central elements of the 512-room hotel are the TWA Flight Center, built in 1962 and used as a terminal until 2001, and the renovated "Jetstream", as the L-1649 was called at TWA, with a redesigned interior and retro-style murals. Following two editions in the larger 1/200 scale, this absolute aviation classic is now also being released in 1/500.
